title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_0LD0LB_1RE0LB_1RF---_0RB0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_0LD0LB_1RE0LB_1RF---_0RB0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of nested counters (segments of ones and of 10s). Both kinds of sweep of the last segment are proved in Lean for every size. An exact accelerated run built on them finds no halt in the first 1.4·1016 steps. The events between batches of sweeps, where a segment runs out and the one before it ticks, are read off the simulation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 66,103 cells have been visited and 44,834 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweep
claims.text: The pieces of a sweep (wall_right, ones_left, fill) and the two whole sweeps, for every size and any tape to the left. Mode Q: L 1^4 (10)^(b+2) 0 1 0 0 (10)^(c+1) A> to L (10)^(b+4) 0 1 0 0 (10)^(c+2) A> in 8b + 4c + 38 steps. Mode P: L 1 1 (10)^(b+1) A> to L (10)^(b+3) A> in 4b + 10 steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.39·10<sup>16</sup> steps
claims.text: c/accel.c does every sweep that one of the two proved rules covers in batches, with the proved step counts, and simulates everything else step by step. It agrees with the plain machine at the sweep ends at steps 59,136,370, 111,168,816 and 2,401,664,914. It runs 13,977,446,236,662,410 steps without a halt, in 10 seconds, with 136,198,641 sweeps in 78 batches; the tape is then 272,397,888 cells long.

claims.title: A hierarchy of counters
claims.text: The events between batches follow a cycle per segment. A segment 1^x (10)^9 ticks four times (4 ones fewer, 2 10s more each time) while its small companion goes through the shapes 0.4, 2.3, 2.4, 4.4, 0.6, 10.1 and 6.3. Then it freezes, and the new last segment, about three times as long, starts the same cycle. Later segments also show other companion shapes (2.5, 6.4), depending on residues. Read off the event log of the accelerated run; not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if the nested counters ever produce a shape that leads to E reading 1; which shapes do is not known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape of this machine is a list of counters, each a block of ones followed by a block of 10s. The head wears the last one down four ones at a time. When it is used up, the counter before it ticks once and a new, longer last counter is built, like the digits of an odometer.

facts.text: No halt in an exact accelerated run that batches the proved sweeps.
No halt in the C simulator; 66,103 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
One sweep of the last counter, in either of its two modes, proved in Lean for every size.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.49).
After 109 steps the tape spans 66,103 cells (21 left of the start, 48,691 right), with a density of 1s of 0.678.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Counters inside counters
html: A few million steps in, the tape reads 1^385 (10)^15 0 1^4 (10)^4 0 1^466 (10)^17 0 … 0 1^a (10)^b 0 1 0 0 (10)^c. Each sweep eats four ones of the last block of ones, adds two 10 pairs after it and one at the end. Lean proves this for every size.

When the last block of ones is gone, the segment before it ticks: it has four ones fewer and two 10 pairs more. The 10 blocks on the right are then rebuilt into a new block of ones, about three times longer than before. Earlier segments change more and more rarely, like the higher digits of a counter.

Because the sweeps are proved rules with exact step counts, a simulator can do thousands of them at once and only step through the rare events by hand. That gets the run from blank tape to 1.4·1016 steps in ten seconds, still without a halt. By then the tape is 272 million cells long: a row of big counters, each holding millions of ones, each with a small companion of a few cells. A counter ticks four times, its companion changing shape each time, and then it freezes while a new counter about three times longer takes over at the end. The machine can halt only during one of these events, and what decides it is the exact shapes and residues of the counters.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Nested counters of 1s and 10s ticked by sweeps that are proved in Lean; an exact accelerated run finds no halt in the first 1.4·10^16 steps.
